chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in the Replacement (recompense from God) will be generous in giving.'

key_terms.الخلف: The Replacement/Recompense — God's promise to replace what is given in charity with something better (cf. Quran 34:39: 'He will replace it')
key_terms.العطية: The act of giving, charitable gift, donation

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the connection between faith in God's reward and generosity in charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits this saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) which links theological conviction to practical generosity. The word 'al-khalaf' (the Replacement) refers to God's promise to replace what is given in charity with something better — a divine guarantee that one who gives will not be left without. This hadith thus motivates charitable giving by grounding it in faith: the believer who truly trusts God's promise of recompense will not hesitate to give generously.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is certain of the Replacement would be generous with the giving’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘One who is certain of (good) consequences, he strives to make it a good gift.’”
